WITH telescope_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    observstation,
    COUNT(*) AS num_telescopes,
    AVG(bandusagepct) AS avg_bandwidth
  FROM telescopes
  GROUP BY observstation
),
all_observatories AS (
  SELECT 
    o.observstation,
    COALESCE(ts.num_telescopes, 0) AS num_telescopes,
    ts.avg_bandwidth
  FROM observatories o
  LEFT JOIN telescope_stats ts ON o.observstation = ts.observstation
),
avg_telescope_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(num_telescopes) AS avg_count
  FROM all_observatories
)
SELECT 
  ao.observstation,
  ao.avg_bandwidth,
  ao.num_telescopes,
  ao.num_telescopes / atc.avg_count AS ratio
FROM all_observatories ao
CROSS JOIN avg_telescope_count atc
ORDER BY ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The denominator ('average telescope count across all those stations') includes observatories with zero telescopes, not just those with at least one telescope. This follows directly from the request: 'For every observatory station in observatories, including stations with no telescopes... that number divided by the average telescope count across all those stations.' The phrase 'all those stations' refers back to 'every observatory station... including stations with no telescopes.'
Observatories with zero telescopes show NULL for average bandwidth (not 0), since there is no data to average. The request specifies 'have no average bandwidth' for such stations.
